problem_statement: The Milosian blog-template project is a small static editorial photography blog for PresleyFrame.com (Hugo Presley) with a fixed masthead, a hero, a 'My recent posts' section with three photo-essay cards, and a reader-focus filter panel that narrows the essays by topic (All posts / Summertime / Travel Frames / Studio Notes). Grow the reader-focus idea into a shared design-system component: (1) build out the real Blog and About pages (blog.html, about.html) that were previously empty, and (2) add a shared 'Reader focus rail' to the site FOOTER of EVERY page (home, blog, about) so readers can jump to a photo-essay theme from anywhere, styled to match the reader-focus filter panel. The rail must appear consistently on all three pages. Keep the on-page reader-focus filter wired end to end: clicking a topic chip (Travel Frames / Studio Notes) must update the 'Showing N posts' status readout to reflect the selected topic (e.g. clicking Travel Frames sets 'Showing 1 post: Iranian portrait walk.'), not merely highlight the chip and hide cards. The filter panel and rail must keep the quiet dark teal editorial look (black panels, teal accents, Playfair typography) matching the reference design, and must be responsive so the home page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport. Preserve the PresleyFrame identity, navigation, hero, post cards, local imagery, and the desktop/tablet layout.
required_content: Keep the reader-focus filter panel (eyebrow 'REGRESSION CONTINUITY', heading 'Reader focus controls', and the four topic chips All posts / Summertime / Travel Frames / Studio Notes) on the home page.

Build the real Blog (blog.html) and About (about.html) pages with the PresleyFrame masthead and navigation, and add the shared 'Reader focus rail' component (eyebrow 'READER FOCUS RAIL' + theme links) to the FOOTER of ALL THREE pages (home, blog, about) so the same reader-focus component appears consistently site-wide, not only on the home page.

Style the filter strip and the shared rail to match the reference dark teal editorial look (black/teal panels, teal-outlined chips, Playfair typography) — the rendered filter panel must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette restyle.

Make the filter strip responsive so the home page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport (allow the chips to wrap / use a fluid layout instead of a fixed-width non-wrapping row). Do not merely clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width.
Keep the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts free of horizontal overflow.

Keep the reader-focus filter fully wired end to end: clicking a topic chip (Travel Frames / Studio Notes / All posts) must update the '.filter-status' 'Showing N posts' readout to reflect the selected topic (e.g. clicking Travel Frames yields 'Showing 1 post: Iranian portrait walk.'), in addition to highlighting the active chip and hiding non-matching cards — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected topic, not the default 'Showing 3 posts'.
Do not damage the existing PresleyFrame masthead, Hugo Presley hero, 'My recent posts' section, the three post cards, local images, or navigation; keep the branding on every page.
design_constraints: Keep the quiet dark editorial PresleyFrame visual language: black backgrounds, teal accent (#42a4b8), Playfair Display typography, rounded panels, teal shadows, fixed dark masthead.
Do not replace the blog, the reader-focus filter, or the pages with a new app shell, framework, external design system, or unrelated layout.
Do not remove the reader-focus filter panel, the four topic chips, the shared footer rail, the post cards, the hero, the navigation, or the filter script.
Do not add npm dependencies, remote scripts, remote fonts, remote images, generated build outputs, or unrelated file churn.
The filter strip and rail must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, and must render in the PresleyFrame teal editorial palette.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial verify the original photography-blog shell and repaired responsive layout across breakpoints.
desktop_reader_focus_component and mobile_reader_focus_component verify the new filter component is visible inside the recent-posts section.
desktop_travel_filter and mobile_travel_filter click Travel Frames and verify the focused one-post status and filtered card state.
desktop_studio_filter clicks Studio Notes and verifies the second one-post filter state.
desktop_all_posts_reset clicks a focused state and returns to All posts with all three cards visible.
desktop_post_cards_regression verifies the original post-card area, images, and read-more links remain present after the component extension.

change_completion: The reader-focus filter panel and its four topic chips remain on the home page.
The shared 'Reader focus rail' appears in the footer of all three pages (home, blog, about).
On mobile the home page has no horizontal overflow after the responsive layout.
content_asset_continuity: The posts stay grounded in the repo's local images (butterfly, iranian, man-painting); no external or placeholder media.
The PresleyFrame masthead, hero, post cards, and navigation are preserved.
design_consistency: The filter strip and shared rail keep the dark teal editorial style and are visually faithful to the reference.
The same reader-focus component is consistent across all three pages; the hero, cards, and masthead remain recognizable.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a topic chip updates the 'Showing N posts' status readout to the selected topic (the post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
The All posts reset restores the full three-post view and status.
regression: Home, blog, and about pages retain the PresleyFrame branding, nav labels, and imagery.
No new dependency, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced.
responsive: The home page has no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile states.
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow.

scoring_notes: A correct patch extends the existing recent-posts component with real filter interaction and targeted responsive regression repair. Static labels without click behavior, filters that delete cards from the source, missing default/travel/studio status text, broken mobile layout, replaced local images, removed hero/header/post cards/read-more links, new dependencies, or remote media should fail completion, regression, responsive, asset, or source checks.
author_notes: Slot 305 targets the Milosian blog-template repository for editorial_blog / Regression Continuity / extend_interaction / component / L3. The task is intentionally component-scoped but includes an explicit mobile regression repair because the original static template positions hero content with a viewport-height margin that is fragile on narrow screens.
